newsitem.title: USA: Ark. Gov says job creation key to welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Ark. Gov says job creation key to welfare reform.

text.p: Arkansas Governor Mike Huckabee sees the new federal welfare reform mandate as "one of those good news, bad news situations."

"The good new is now the federal government finally realizes their attempts after 31 years and $5 trillion dollars is a colossal failure," Huckabee, a Republican, told reporters gathered at a New York luncheon where he was promoting his state.
"The bad news is, after they realize it, they toss it back to the states and it's in our lap, and we have two years to do what they failed to do in 31," he said.
Job creation is the key to the welfare reform, Huckabee said.
Welfare benefits in Arkansas can amount to as much as $8 an hour, if rent subsidies, food stamps and various other programs open to an individual with children are figured in, he said.
"Why would anyone want to take that level of benefits...tax free, and exchange that for a minimum wage job upon which you are going to pay taxes," Huckabee said. "It doesn't make sense."

Arkansas needs to find a way to get welfare recipients jobs that will not result in a substantially lower living standard, he said. To help achieve that, the public and private sectors must work together, he said.
Huckabee said he met recently with representatives of nursing homes from across the state. That industry needs 8,000 to 10,000 new employees each year, he said.
"These are entry level jobs," the Governor said. "They are jobs that have training associated with (them)."

Another idea would be employer incentives. For instance, an employer's portion of the hourly wage might be $3 with the state providing the remaining $5 to $6, Huckabee said. Such an opportunity would allow an unskilled worker a chance to "learn a work ethic," and practice it, the Governor said.
Past attempts to allieviate poverty through various programs have made an "industry" of it, he said.
"We have created a lot of government, not to help people out of poverty but to provide vendors a place through which they can have a job," Huckabee said.
An ordained Baptist minister, Huckabee became Arkansas'44th governor with the resignation of Governor Jim Guy Tucker on July 15.
